mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without any regime condition.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0%, or the Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS rise, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), the tight labor market supports consumer spending and corporate profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals robust labor market conditions that enhance consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when PAYEMS rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, it indicates a tight labor market that supports strong consumer demand and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate coupled with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates a falling real interest rate, which reduces the cost of capital and stimulates equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 310), a rise in the federal funds rate signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases real rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 310 and FEDFUNDS rises, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
